screens.penny: Hi, {name}! Cheapest isn't always best. Let's see why.

screens.title: How long does it last?

cards.caption: Something well made can last a long time.
The cheapest thing can break quickly.

screens.penny: We look at the price AND how long it lasts, {name}.

screens.story: One pair of shoes costs 4 coins and wears out fast. Another costs 6 coins and lasts a year.
screens.pennyHint: Think about how long each one lasts, {name}.

options.label: The 6-coin pair
options.outcome: The shoes last all year. Kai does not have to buy another pair.

options.label: The 4-coin pair
options.outcome: The cheap shoes wear out in a month. Kai has to buy another pair, and spends more in the end.

screens.rightMessage: Yes, {name}! Paying a bit more can cost less in the end.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! The cheap pair wears out, so Kai buys shoes twice.

screens.prompt: Kai bought the 4-coin shoes twice. Count what he really spent.
screens.rightMessage: That's 8 coins, {name}! The 6-coin pair would have cost less.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! He paid 4 coins, then 4 again. Let's count all 8.

screens.prompt: Is the cheapest thing always the best choice?
screens.rightMessage: That's right, {name}! Sometimes it costs more in the end.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! Kai's cheap shoes cost him more, because he bought them twice.
screens.retryIntro: Let's think about the cheapest choice again, {name}.

screens.title: Great thinking, {name}!
screens.message: Look at the price and how long it lasts.
